brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: 6 piece bases placed: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,0,1;full (stacked), piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full, piece:-1,0,0;half-e – meshClash clear
No bin parts placed (counts show 0 bins). Sockets exist for hex-bin-* bins at -1,0,0, 0,1,0, 1,-1,0, 1,0,0 etc., but none installed in time.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut (w:slide) on half-e at -1,0,0 – provided by addDrawer at -1,0,0 key w
No handle present. find_sockets handle =0 – requires a cover on top (e.g., at 0,0,1) to mount handle; no covers installed.

finish.summary: Partial build: base cluster and one slide drawer are complete and mesh-verified (clear). Bins and carry handle could not be completed within turns – bin sockets and handle mounting point (needs cover) remain available but unexecuted.

lines.label: Slide drawer tub (west half, north quarter)
Slide drawer tub (west half, south quarter)
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
